kev_floor.justification: KEV listing means exploitation has been confirmed in the wild, so a reachable KEV CVE should never rank as unlikely because of a low EPSS. This matters most for water: of the KEV-listed CVEs that also have a CISA ICS advisory in the water sector, half have EPSS below 0.1 (median 0.09, 16 CVEs, a small sample). Across all ICS KEV entries EPSS is not lower than KEV overall (median 0.67 vs 0.57), so the floor is a water-sector correction, not a general ICS one. 0.5 treats a reachable KEV CVE as at least a coin flip.
kev_floor.source: CISA KEV catalog (BOD 22-01): a CVE is only added with evidence of active exploitation. EPSS figures: CISA KEV v2026.10.29 joined with the jgamblin/KEV_EPSS mirror (30 Oct 2026). The 0.5 value itself is a design choice.

default_credentials.justification: Default passwords are public and tried automatically by scanners and botnets; failure mostly comes from the device being changed or unreachable, not from difficulty.
default_credentials.source: Joint advisory AA23-335A (Dec 2023): IRGC-affiliated actors compromised internet-exposed Unitronics PLCs, including at US water facilities, likely by exploiting poor password security such as default passwords. Supports "this happens in practice", not the 0.9 number.

exposed_remote_access_no_mfa.justification: Needs a working credential (guessing, stuffing or a leaked password), so harder than defaults but realistic over time for an internet-facing service.

likelihood_scale.justification: EPSS values differ by orders of magnitude, so a log scale keeps differences visible. The bounds are fixed, not taken from the current assets, so changing one asset never moves another asset's score.

anomaly_boost_alpha.justification: An anomaly is a signal, not proof of compromise. A score of 1.0 closes 30% of the remaining gap to certainty (p' = p + (1 - p) × 0.3 × score), so the ML raises priority without overriding the vulnerability evidence.

mfa_reduction_factor.justification: Deliberately more conservative than vendor headline figures, because targeted attackers bypass MFA (push fatigue, session/token theft).
mfa_reduction_factor.source: Microsoft Security blog (Aug 2019) reported that accounts using MFA are over 99.9% less likely to be compromised; we use 90% to allow for targeted bypass. The 0.1 value is a design choice.

consequence_weights.justification: Physical safety dominates in critical infrastructure; people affected comes next; duration matters but is partly captured by the other two.
consequence_weights.source: Consequence-first framing follows INL's Consequence-driven Cyber-informed Engineering (CCE). The weights themselves are a design choice.

consequence_normalisation.formula: Severity ÷ 4; people affected ÷ 500,000 (city population); outage hours ÷ 72 (longest outage in the scenario); each capped at 1
consequence_normalisation.justification: Puts each component on 0–1 before weighting. People affected is the largest people_served among services lost, not the sum (see consequence_numbers.md, rule 4), so overlapping populations are not double-counted.

opportunistic.name: Opportunistic Cybercriminal
opportunistic.cve_filter: Only uses edges whose best CVE is KEV-listed or has EPSS >= 0.1, or that are a default-credential weakness
opportunistic.justification: Mass-scanning attackers go for exposed, known-exploited weaknesses and default passwords, and do not chain long paths into OT.
opportunistic.source: Design choice, consistent with MITRE ATT&CK for ICS campaigns C0031 (Unitronics, 2023) and C0066 (U.S. water utilities, 2026), both listing T0883 Internet Accessible Device and T1694.001 Default Credentials

nation_state.name: State-Sponsored APT
nation_state.justification: Patient, well-resourced actors chain through IT and DMZ into control layers and use third-party access.

insider.name: Disgruntled / Compromised Insider
insider.justification: Models an employee or a stolen employee account: no need to break in, only to move laterally.

patch_it.justification: Standard OS/app patch plus a reboot, usually possible within the month.

patch_ot.justification: Firmware updates on controllers need vendor validation, testing and a process shutdown, so they are deferred (patchable_now = false).

segment_rule.justification: Rule change plus testing that operations traffic still flows; no process stop needed.

disable_remote_access.justification: Quick to switch off; the cost is operational (vendor support must be re-arranged), noted in the UI rather than counted as downtime.

add_mfa.justification: Enrolment and testing for the remote-access gateway users.

enhanced_monitoring.justification: Detection, not prevention: raises confidence, does not lower likelihood.
